title: Force Over Area
description: The Baron's vault door resists brute force. Professor Mass reveals the secret: it's not just force that matters, but force spread over area — pressure.

content.value: The same force can feel very different depending on the area it acts over. PRESSURE is the force acting on a unit area of a surface.

force
Pressure = ─────────
             area

Smaller area  → MORE pressure
Larger area   → LESS pressure  (for the same force)

Press your palm flat against your desk — barely a mark. Now press with a single fingertip using the same effort — it hurts more! The force is similar, but the fingertip spreads it over a tiny area, so the pressure is much higher.

Force is measured in newtons (N) and area in square metres (m²). So pressure is measured in newtons per square metre (N/m²), also called the PASCAL (Pa). One pascal is quite small, so we often use larger units for real-world pressures.
To INCREASE pressure, reduce the area (use a sharp point). To DECREASE pressure, increase the area (use a wide, flat surface).
Key Takeaway: Pressure = force ÷ area. For the same force, a smaller area gives more pressure and a larger area gives less. Pressure is measured in pascals (N/m²).

quiz.question: Pressure is defined as…
quiz.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area. The same force over a smaller area gives more pressure.

quiz.question: For the same force, using a SMALLER area produces…
quiz.explain: Pressure = force / area, so shrinking the area increases the pressure.

quiz.question: The SI unit of pressure is the…
quiz.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa), which is newtons per square metre (N/m²).
